text: Figure 9.16: Editor view of Client-Server Interface Operation Definition » As depicted in the Figures ( 5.16, 5.16) above, a ClientServerInterface is composed of ClientServerOperations, i.e. a ClientServerOperation cannot be reused in the con- text of a different ClientServerInterface. A ClientServerOperation may contain 0 to many ArgumentDataPrototypes. The latter may be • passed to the operation • passed to and returned from the operation • Returned from the operation. Example: In the above screen shot, a client/server interface "T rsmRatGear1" is defined to return the gear ratio for a given gear, the client requests the operation ’GetT rsmRat- Gear’ with input argument ’Gear’. The function call returns the output argument ’Rat’. In AUTOSAR CP (and AP), client-server operations are defined as: Operations declared within the scope of a client/server interface. For AUTOSAR FO, the following definition is applied: A remote procedure call declared within the scope of the current interface. Arguments: The Arguments of a client-server interface operation can be seen as own interfaces of the operation. When the operation of the interface is called the arguments transport the concerned information which need to be exchanged between the Client (caller) and the Server (callee) SW Component. Arguments are typified by data types and have names and a direction. The Direction defines if the Argument is an input or an output or input and output of the operation.
